描述_EN: the finial decoration is in openwork: on one pin, a lion roars amid leaf scrolls; on the other, a flying bird is seen against a cross-pattern. hairpins also became significantly larger, ranging from 20 to 35 cm (8 to 14 in.) in length. royal and aristocratic women wore buns of false hair decorated with an elaborate array of silver hairpins like these to dazzle and impress. the number of hairpins worn was also indicative of the wearer's social status. as women’s hairstyles became higher and more sophisticated, new types of hair accessories were developed to dress them. the tang dynasty marked the high point in the crafting of gold and silver hair ornaments, with both the technique and style showing the influence of persian and sasanian silverware. both motifs are surrounded by a border of half-palmettes, and further enhanced by the gilding of the pattern areas, a technique that also protects the silver surface from tarnishing. these two hairpins (zan) have been beaten into shape from sheet silver.
描述_ZN: the finial decoration is in openwork: on one pin, a lion roars amid leaf scrolls; on the other, a flying bird is seen against a cross-pattern. 发簪也明显变大，长度从20到35厘米（8到14英寸）不等。 皇室和贵族妇女戴着假发的发髻，上面装饰着像这样精致的银簪子，让人眼花缭乱，印象深刻。 佩戴的发卡数量也表明了佩戴者的社会地位。 随着妇女的发型变得更高、更精致，新类型的发饰也被开发出来，以装扮她们。 唐代标志着金银发饰制作的高潮，其技术和风格都显示了波斯和萨珊银器的影响。 这两个图案都被一个半掌状的边框所包围，并通过对图案区域的镀金来进一步加强，这种技术也能保护银器表面不被玷污。 这两支发簪（Zan）是用银片打成的。
